start.content: You are wasting your time with these questions, scribe. I am Eleazar. I saw the whole 'procession' from my villa's upper terrace. It was nothing more than a band of lawless Galileans causing a disturbance.

choices.text: What exactly did you see at the tethering post?
The people were celebrating, not rioting.

theft_claim.content: I saw two of them — likely the ones they call the 'sons of thunder' given the noise they were making. They drew a blade, hacked through the rope, and made off with the colt. The owner was clearly terrified.

choices.text: The rope fibers don't look hacked.

aristocrat_view.content: They went toward the gate, dragging the beast along. They were throwing their dirty cloaks in the mud as if the street were a palace floor. It is an insult to the dignity of Jerusalem.

choices.text: Why do you dislike this teacher so much?

rope_evasion.content: Hacked, cut, untied — what does it matter? The animal was removed without a proper transaction. In the eyes of the Law, that is theft.

closing.content: Keep your notes, scribe. But remember: a movement built on a borrowed donkey will not last the week. The Sanhedrin will handle this.
